summary: Publishing a new mission revision automatically supersedes runs already active on stale revisions. Replacement admission is checked before cancellation. Valid replacements retain exact inputs and workspace, wait for ordinary source cleanup to reach terminal, then restart every step and program without journal adoption. Incompatible sources remain active with a visible fault. Native and public readers expose supersession lineage alongside existing retry links.

replay.detail: Append-only mission-run.supersede-linked claims on both endpoints restore source/replacement lineage; existing reconcile.fault claims in scope mission/supersession restore faulted/recovered admission reasons. Publication creates the replacement and ordinarily cancels the source atomically only after admission succeeds. Replaying or republishing an unchanged revision does not create another replacement. A rebuildable member-local dirty-head queue observes actual selected mission head changes, including delayed owned-set promotion. Replacement execution deadlines start at cleanup admission or the retained after-run dependency admission, using accepted claim timestamps on replay.

schema.detail: Register system-only mission-run.supersede-linked with required source and replacement mission-run references and publication string. Extend mission-run.created with optional phase and admission_publication fields and reconcile.fault with optional publication, supporting supersession-waiting replacements and immutable refusal episodes. Add a rebuildable local dirty-head queue and mission-definition head-change triggers. Mission run views and public summaries gain optional non-null supersedes, superseded_by, and supersession_fault strings, omitting absent strings. Generated Rust, Swift, and TypeScript clients retain retry fields and tolerate older responses without supersession fields. No destructive data rewrite.

rules.detail: Registry and retention compatibility digests change for supersession contracts. Replacement preflight uses ordinary start admissibility, exact input declarations and kinds, capacity, interpolation, and original starter authority before cancelling a source. No new DSL grammar or authority grant is introduced.

compatibility.detail: Coordinate participating member upgrades before upgraded owners process stale active runs or new mission publications, because registry and retention digests change. Owner startup can supersede runs against an already-selected newer head; account for this during rollout. Older tolerant clients ignore additive fields; new clients accept older responses with absent fields. Explicit run generations continue to pin code and journal. Same-revision retry after a newer publication is not superseded until a later new revision is published.

downtime.detail: No fleet shutdown or data migration is required. New-revision publication intentionally cancels eligible active stale runs and waits for ordinary finalization and cleanup before replacement work begins; this creates a per-run execution gap. A replacement admission refusal leaves its source running.

manual.detail: Review new revisions for fresh-start compatibility before publishing; supersession is automatic, not opt-in. Make all steps and program effects idempotent against existing workspace and external effects. Inspect missions show or public list/detail/history for supersedes, superseded_by, and supersession_fault. Republish of the same revision alone does nothing.

recovery.detail: Supersession does not undo external effects or erase source history. If admission fails, inspect the source/target revisions and incompatibility in supersession_fault, correct the definition, and publish a new revision. If cleanup is pending, inspect and resolve ordinary source finalization before replacement work can proceed. Stop writing new supersession claims before downgrade and retain durable history; use a compatible owner and reader for in-flight supersession-waiting histories, and restore a compatible build to read new contracts.
